summary: Webhook content-type normalization causes callback idempotency misses (JSON vs CloudEvents)
description: Customer reports duplicate downstream side-effects from function-tool invocations when our webhook callback is delivered with CloudEvents content-type instead of application/json. The idempotency dedup appears to be bypassed because the callback normalizes content-type and payload wrapper differently than the incoming acknowledgement we record, causing separate idempotency signatures.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Customer sends a model request that triggers a tool/function call which returns an async callback URL.
2) Redwood delivers callback POST to customer endpoint with Content-Type: application/json and body {"idempotency_key": "abc123", "status": "completed"}.

3) In some environments the customer's edge layer rewrites webhook to CloudEvents (Content-Type: application/cloudevents+json) and wraps payload into {"specversion":..., "data": { original payload } }.

4) Customer then issues a follow-up retry to the Redwood API referencing the same original idempotency semantics; Redwood receives the callback variation and fails to match to the original recorded callback signature, resulting in duplicate downstream processing.
5) Observed duplicates manifest as repeated 3rd-party webhook deliveries and duplicate database writes on customer side.

investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: idempotency matching uses canonicalization that includes top-level content-type and body shape, so CloudEvents-wrapped callbacks do not normalize to the same canonical signature.
Checked webhook delivery pipeline: delivery service records content-type header and computes idempotency_sig = hash(content-type + canonical_body).
Customer edge is transforming payload into CloudEvents wrapper which changes canonical_body and content-type -> produces different hash.
Confirmed SDKs and server-side code do not currently strip known wrappers (CloudEvents) prior to idempotency signature calculation.
Reproduced locally by running a small HTTP server that rewrites incoming JSON into CloudEvents envelope; observed two distinct idempotency signatures produced by delivery service.
comments: Sofia Gonzalez (Support) 2026-03-10: Customer reported duplicates after a production rollout; they see 2x downstream callbacks for ~12% of requests.
Ethan Brooks (SRE) 2026-03-11: Reproduced on staging. Delivery service computes idempotency_sig using raw headers+body. Edge rewriting explains mismatch.
Customer (ZapFlow) 2026-03-11: We rely on a CloudEvents bridge to unify third-party webhooks; we can disable it but prefer the platform handle normalization.

Ethan Brooks (SRE) 2026-03-12: Proposed mitigation: normalize CloudEvents envelopes (if content-type cloudevents) by extracting .data for canonicalization; creating short-term routing rule to prefer application/json header if present.
Sofia Gonzalez (Support) 2026-03-12: Logged as P1 due to enterprise impact; customer requests ETA on fix and a temporary config flag if possible.
resolution: Workaround provided: toggled delivery-service flag to perform CloudEvents unwrap for callbacks from ZapFlow's IP range and recomputed idempotency matching to align with original signatures. Engineering to implement a robust normalization layer that recognizes common wrappers (CloudEvents, SNS envelope) and uses canonicalized payload for idempotency hashing. Follow-up PR created to add opt-in normalization and documentation in webhook runbook. Customer confirmed duplicates stopped after workaround.
follow_up_actions: ENG: Implement content-type normalization pipeline for webhook callbacks (PR #4821) - owner @ethan
DOCS: Add guidance to webhook runbook about envelope normalization and idempotency behavior
SUPPORT: Offer post-mortem and recommend customers using middleware bridges enable passthrough mode or add original-idempotency header
